subject: MAP slippage: rebaseline proposal and escalation
messages:
From: Elena Varga <procurement@starlabs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@acme-eng.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP milestones slipping — need clarity

Karthik / Laura,

Quick note from procurement: several MAP milestones are showing late signs on our side (integration test window and security evidence delivery). Stakeholders here are concerned about the proposed go-live on 2025-05-02. Can you confirm whether Redwood still expects to meet that date, and what contingencies you can offer?

Specifically:
- Updated ETA for security questionnaires and audit log samples
- Any changes to acceptance window or cutover plan
- If a hard rebaseline is needed, we need an initial proposal by EOD Wednesday (2025-04-16) for our steering committee.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Varga
Head of Procurement, Starlabs
procurement@starlabs.com

Attachments: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Varga <procurement@starlabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestones slipping — need clarity

Elena — thanks for flagging. Short answer: we do not think a hard go/no-go is necessary yet, but we need to realign the MAP (minor rebaseline) and add a short contingency lane. I pulled the most recent MAP and annotated gaps — see attached MAP_v3.xlsx.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can Starlabs confirm the latest acceptable cutover week range (you mentioned early May; is shifting into the week of 5/9 acceptable?)
- Any procurement constraints (final PO date) that would force a different cadence?

I'll loop in Laura and Marcus for capacity and SLA exception checks. Proposed next steps:
1) Internal triage (today) to size tech impact
2) Joint sync with Starlabs Wed 4/16 for approval of rebaseline
3) Executive note to legal/procurement if SLA exception or contract amendment is required

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, annotated)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Rebaseline ask and exec hold point

Karthik / Marcus — quick internal: I've reviewed Elena's note and the MAP draft. Two items to escalate now:

1) Procurement constraint: Starlabs needs a signed addendum before their internal board on 2025-05-01; if we delay acceptance beyond 4/23 this becomes tight.
2) SLA exception: the current latency target for the production model will need a temporary relaxation during initial ramp unless we commit dedicated capacity. Legal will need an exception packet.

Options I recommend:
- Option A (preferred): Commit a dedicated 2x GPU burst pool for first 30 days; update MAP to shift go-live to week of 5/12 to buy two weeks for audit evidence and final integration. This requires an SLA exception packet and a one-off credit (I can take exec approval for a <10% credit).
- Option B: Keep go-live 5/2, deliver mitigations (prefix caching, smaller batch size) and accept a temporary latency penalty during peak test windows — much higher operational risk.

We need Marcus to confirm feasibility and perf impact by EOD today so I can prepare the SLA exception with Legal. Marcus?

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: INTERNAL: Rebaseline ask and exec hold point

Laura / Karthik — technical readout:

Summary: Option A (dedicated burst capacity + shift to 5/12) is the safest. We can stage a short warmup plan to prime KV caches and pre-cache expected prefixes; that should reduce token cost and latency for initial acceptance tests. If budget prevents dedicated pool, Option B is feasible but will likely show 20-30% higher p95 latency during integration testing and a non-trivial risk of throttled throughput.

Concrete deliverables I can commit to if Option A chosen:
- Prefetch script and cache warmup runbook (2 business days to prepare)
- Canary configuration with automatic fallback to quantized model variant on sustained latency breaches
- Audit log dump (sample) by 4/18 for procurement/security review

Dependencies: confirm capacity (ops) and approval of one-off credit for the dedicated pool. I'll coordinate with infra once Laura confirms exec decision.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Varga <procurement@starlabs.com>, Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@acme-eng.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Apr 2025 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestones slipping — need clarity

Elena / Rajesh — thanks for the patience. Following internal triage, proposed rebaseline and escalation path below. This is our formal recommendation to the Starlabs steering committee:

Proposed rebaseline (preferred)
- New target cutover week: 2025-05-12 (two-week slip)
- Contingency lane: Dedicated burst capacity (2x GPU pool) for first 30 days of production
- Audit evidence: sample logs and SOC-lite bundle delivered by 2025-04-18
- Acceptance window: maintain 10 business day validation, with a soft freeze on major schema changes during validation

Action items (owners / ETA)
- Redwood (Marcus): Cache warmup runbook + canary config — 2025-04-17
- Redwood (Karthik): Draft SLA exception addendum and credit proposal — 2025-04-17 EOD
- Starlabs (Elena): Confirm acceptable cutover range (5/12 preferred) and any PO hard-dates — 2025-04-16 EOD
- Legal / Procurement (joint): Review SLA addendum — target 4/23

Attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx (annotated), SLA_exception_request.pdf (draft)

If Starlabs confirms 5/12 as acceptable, we'll prepare the exec summary and route the SLA packet for sign-off. If you need a shorter window we can discuss limited mitigations but that increases risk (detailed above).

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
